clue.text: Playing snooker abandoned for help to the gardener?

blocks.note: potting balls is what you do when playing snooker
to shed something is to cast it off

explanation.surface: Someone gives up their game of snooker to go and lend a hand in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden shed where seedlings are potted up is a building that serves anyone working on plants and flowers.

clue.text: Pointless 14, around a street at home, is the 23 7

definitions.note: the thief of time: the whole proverb is 'procrastination is the thief of time'

indicators.note: a point is a compass letter, so pointless asks for that letter of the cross-referenced word to go
around says the shortened word wraps itself round the next pieces

blocks.note: 14 across is defined as 'generative state', which is also this word
taken as written
standard abbreviation for street
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A cross-referenced riddle completing a famous proverb about putting things off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointless 14' does not use 14's answer: it uses another word for 14's definition, and the point removed is E, East on the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Young's proverb says delay steals our hours: putting tasks off is what robs us of our time.

clue.text: Healthy bread?

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: a drink to someone's health

blocks.note: first meaning: a drink proposed to someone's good health
second meaning: bread browned under the grill

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a question about wholemeal loaves; 'healthy' really points to raising a glass to someone's health.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast is both a salute drunk to someone's wellbeing and slices of bread browned by heat.

clue.text: Doing nothing for a moment?

definitions.note: the word that completes 'moment of ...' in physics

blocks.note: first meaning: idleness, a lack of will to act
second meaning: physics speaks of the moment of this quantity, resistance to rotation

explanation.walkthrough: 'For a moment' looks like 'briefly', but it means the word that goes with moment in the physics term moment of inertia.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia means sluggish inactivity, and the moment of inertia is a body's resistance to turning in mechanics.

clue.text: Is he top of de range?

definitions.note: the adjective stands for a noun here, as in 'one of the top', fair because a top person is a grandee

indicators.note: read as one word, derange means to throw into disorder, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: the two words run together; they are both the signal and the letters themselves

explanation.surface: A mock-foreign question asking whether a man is the best of his range or class.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that 'de range' is derange, which both supplies the letters and tells you to jumble them.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a Spanish nobleman of the highest rank, hence any person of eminence and importance.

clue.text: Another top in the county, very brief

definitions.note: an adjective describing the garment; the answer is a noun

indicators.note: another version of the word means its letters rearranged into a different form
in places the jumbled word inside the county

blocks.note: the word top with its letters mixed
Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county

explanation.surface: A fashion note about yet another skimpy top seen around the county.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampshire, a county in southern England, is written Hants. A top is a garment, but the answer is worn below.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot pants are extremely short shorts, so as garments they are famously skimpy and revealing.

clue.text: Translation of 10 16 down's work made a hit with confused committee

indicators.note: made means fashioned or built, so these letters are formed into something new

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, despite looking like a signal
taken as written

explanation.surface: A translated work became a success thanks to a muddled committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' looks like the signal but is part of the letters; 'made' is the signal. 10 (Antonio) translates to Anthony and 16 down is Powell. The final OF TIME is written in 7 down, which has no clue of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dance to the Music of Time is Anthony Powell's twelve-novel sequence, named after a Poussin painting.

clue.text: Dirty gold acted on pole

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so the pole goes after the gold and the acting

blocks.note: S for south, one of the poles
or is gold in heraldry
to act is to do

explanation.surface: Someone did something grubby with gold on a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: The pole is written first: 'on' tells you the other pieces sit after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sordid means squalid or morally base, the same as filthy or grubby in a figurative sense.

clue.text: Distance and time on film

blocks.note: a foot is a unit of length
an age is a long period

explanation.surface: A note on how much length and running time a reel of movie takes up.
explanation.definitionFit: Footage is recorded material from a camera, originally measured by the length of the reel.

clue.text: Merchant with a fanciful notion

indicators.note: fanciful means imaginative and unreal, so these letters are reimagined into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trader who has a strange idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's title character in The Merchant of Venice is called Antonio, the one who borrows from Shylock.

clue.text: Irish girl and boy are annoyed

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for Irish
a girl's name
a boy's name

explanation.surface: An Irish couple are both cross about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritated is a synonym meaning vexed or exasperated, made cross by something.

clue.text: Early idea: the foam must be recycled

indicators.note: recycled material is broken down and remade, so these letters are reprocessed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the colon

explanation.surface: An eco-minded instruction that the foam packaging has to go back for recycling.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram makes AHEAD OF TIME; the OF TIME part is written in 7 down, which has no clue of its own and is shared with 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahead of time is an idiom meaning before the expected or scheduled moment, hence premature.

clue.text: Breaking solvers' back, like, is no problem!

indicators.note: back here means turned backwards, so the word for solvers is read right to left
breaking into something means splitting it open and getting inside

blocks.note: the setter addresses solvers as you, in the old form
like and as are interchangeable in comparisons

explanation.surface: A chatty claim that something which breaks solvers' backs is, like, totally fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like' looks like a verbal tic, but it supplies the inserted word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something easy presents no difficulty at all, which is what the casual phrase claims.

clue.text: Generative state with a lot of brackets: do nothing in retirement

indicators.note: a lot of, not all of, so only the front part of the word is kept
retiring means withdrawing or going back, so these words are read in reverse

blocks.note: round brackets are called parentheses
taken as written
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A writer's style so full of brackets that it stalls, doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a mother or father is the condition that follows from producing offspring, hence a generative state.

clue.text: Expected to show one's free

indicators.note: putting on a show means displaying things in a new arrangement, so the letters are laid out afresh

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone was expected to prove that they are no longer tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something foreseen has been anticipated in advance, which is what expected means as a past participle.

clue.text: Being there from the start with a proper golden face

blocks.note: prim means stiffly proper
or is gold in heraldry
a clock's face is its dial

explanation.surface: Someone present from the outset, with a neat and gilded appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Primordial means existing from the very beginning of time, original and earliest.

clue.text: River, supply of water to Baden?

definitions.note: what is added to Baden to complete a name

blocks.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: A river supplying water to Baden, the German spa region.
explanation.walkthrough: Baden is not the German region: added to it, the answer gives Baden-Powell, founder of the Boy Scouts. It is also the novelist of 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Baden-Powell founded Scouting, so this surname is what attaches to Baden in his double-barrelled name.

clue.text: The cat and the Queen had briefly retired to put on fancy clothes

indicators.note: retired means went back or withdrew, so the run of words is read in reverse

blocks.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat
ER, Elizabeth Regina
had shortens to 'd, as in she'd

explanation.surface: The cat and the Queen both went off to bed in order to change into costumes.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress up is to don costume or smart outfits, an idiom for wearing special clothing.

clue.text: A Catholic, about a month in France, uses a Semitic tongue

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the Catholic abbreviation goes round the month

blocks.note: taken as written
RC, Roman Catholic
taken as written
mai is French for May

explanation.surface: A Catholic spending a month in France speaks an ancient Semitic language.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is an ancient language of the Semitic family, spoken by Jesus and still used today.

clue.text: Revolutionary note in the kitchen

definitions.note: describes where the answer, a person, works

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary
F is a musical note

explanation.surface: A note of revolt pinned up in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook, the person you find at work among the stoves of a restaurant.

clue.text: Have babies in a distant line

blocks.note: far means distant
a row is a line

explanation.surface: Giving birth in a far-off queue.
explanation.definitionFit: To farrow is to give birth to a litter of piglets, the verb used for a sow producing young.

clue.text: The Prince in the Guardian is the big one

indicators.note: in places the prince inside the newspaper's word for itself

blocks.note: Prince Hal, the young Henry V in Shakespeare
a newspaper's editorial voice speaks of itself as we

explanation.surface: A royal story printed in the Guardian is the paper's big scoop.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue appeared in the Guardian, so the paper is 'we' in its own pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales are the largest animals on Earth, so this creature is the big one of the sea.

clue.text: It's like rubber, the beer - send it back to a town near Calais ...

indicators.note: sending back something means returning it, so the drink's word runs backwards

blocks.note: ale is a kind of beer
Saint-Omer, written St Omer, is a French town inland from Calais

explanation.surface: A complaint that the beer tastes like rubber, so return it to a French brewery town.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots carry the French town into the next two clues, where 'whose' refers to it.
explanation.definitionFit: An elastomer is any polymer with elastic properties, the class of material that includes natural rubber.

clue.text: He will take if the possibility is available

indicators.note: a possibility is one possible way among several, so the letters can be arranged another way

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a man who grabs things whenever the chance is there.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: opportunity makes a robber.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber is someone who helps himself to other people's property, so he takes what isn't his.

clue.text: ... whose law on disturbed rest is dawdling (intentionally?) ...

definitions.note: a verb phrase in the third person, like the answer; the question nods to loitering with intent

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the next word's letters are jumbled

blocks.note: whose refers to the French town of the previous clue, so law is in French
the word rest rearranged

explanation.surface: A French town whose bylaws about rest look like a loitering law.
explanation.walkthrough: Loitering with intent is a British criminal offence of hanging about planning a crime, hence the bracketed query.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to linger idly or hang about aimlessly, which dawdling also means.

clue.text: ... and whose upper-class type with love at heart became a poet

indicators.note: at heart means in the middle, so one letter is set inside the other word

blocks.note: the French town makes it a French aristocrat, an aristo
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A French town's toff, a romantic at heart, took up poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludovico Ariosto was the Italian Renaissance writer of the epic Orlando Furioso.

clue.text: General produces, as a trial, Kipling's poem in not quite nice setting

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the final letter is dropped
a setting holds a jewel, so the shortened word surrounds the others

blocks.note: doing something on spec means trying it speculatively
If is Kipling's best-known poem
taken as written

explanation.surface: An army general tries out a Kipling poem in a not-so-pleasant setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-specific means vague and broad rather than particular, matching general as an adjective.
